item.title: His Horrorcore Lyrics Became Reality
item.description: Richard McCroskey, who performed as Syko Sam, traveled from California to Virginia after meeting Emma Niederbrock online. In 2009, he killed Emma, her mother, her father and her friend. He later pleaded guilty to four murders and received four life sentences.

item.title: The Murder That Turned Corpsewood Manor Into A Legend
item.description: In 1982, Dr. Charles Scudder and Joseph Odom were murdered at their secluded Georgia home by two men who believed they were hiding a fortune there. The killings sparked sensational stories about Satanism and the occult, helping turn Corpsewood Manor into a lasting true crime legend.

item.title: The Millionaire Killer Behind Three Murders
item.description: Dellen Millard was convicted of murdering Tim Bosma, Laura Babcock and his father, Wayne Millard. Prosecutors presented the killings as part of a series of calculated schemes involving money, relationships and eliminating people who stood in his way.

item.title: The Cult Leader Who Ruled Through Fear
item.description: Roch Thériault founded the Ant Hill Kids in 1977 and claimed to be a prophet, eventually isolating followers in a remote Canadian commune. His rule involved severe abuse and violence, and he was convicted of second-degree murder in 1993 and sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: He Was Executed Despite Evidence He Was Innocent
item.description: Joe Arridy was executed in Colorado in 1939 after confessing to the murder of 15-year-old Dorothy Drain. He had an IQ of 46, and evidence later showed his confession was coerced and he likely was not in Pueblo when the crime occurred. In 2011, he received a full posthumous pardon.
